chapter: Army band, Lena Horne, Billie Holiday and the 1950s
title: Backing Lena Horne with a small band at the Capitol Theatre
summary: At Chez Paris and the Capitol with Xavier Cugat on the bill, Horace assembled Sid Catlett, Billy Taylor, Al Casey, Dick Vance, Benny Morton, Buddy Bostic and Edmond Hall at about $3,000 a week, paid by MGM.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: How was she to work with?

She was a princess. We played the Chez Paris in Chicago, and I got a group together to back her, and (unintelligible) was terrific. And then we began to rehearse to go into an MGM House, the Capitol Theatre in New York City, and Xavier Cugat, Robert Walker, and Lena Horne on the same bill.

So when Lena heard Xavier Cugat's band was gonna play for her, she said, 'Hom, I don't know if this is gonna be -- we called each other Hom, you know, that was a little slang expression.' 'I don't know if this is gonna work or not.' She says, 'Why don't you go ahead and get a small group together to back me,' you know. So I went ahead and went to New York, and you know, the personnel that I got -- do you wanna hear it?
I got Big Sid Catlett on drums. I got a bass player named Billie Taylor, not the pianist. I got a guitar player named Al Casey.
I think I've heard that name.

Yeah, he was great around New York. That was my rhythm section. I got an excellent little trumpet player named Dick Vance on trumpet. I got Benny Morton on trombone. I got Earl Bostick on clarinet and saxophone, and who was the other guy? Edmond Hall for the other clarinet player.

So I had two clarinets, a muted trumpet, and a trombone, and played light things for Lena, and it swung. And All I had Xavier Cugat's band do during our four weeks stay was on the end, when we finished playing, was to hit the chord.

And this was it. But it was a great thing. You know what that band -- financially, you know what those eight pieces cost? But MGM had to pay for it. They were a little sore, but we played a lot of theatres, and Lena got good money for all the theatres that we played, like the Balabay and Katz BMK in Chicago, (inaudible) and all around, but the Capitol Theatre was an MGM house, and she couldn't go in there on a percentage, she had to take a flat salary, and this is rather Catlett teed her off a little bit, what (unintelligible) so she didn't feel anything about these salaries. Sid Kaplan got $500 a week. Benny Morton asked for
$350, and guys got $400 and all like that. This little They piece band, but it costs $3,000, you know? A week.
Boy, were the heads (Unaudible) really mad about it, but she didn't care.

It was a great thing though. Lena had a great sound. We played light behind her. We had light swing and it moved, because she was so soft, the way she sang, and commanded an audience, you know. It was just beautiful. Then on the end, the great Xavier Cugat's band with the big chord. So that was that.
